259	def gen_group(
260	    rng: random.Random, group_id: str, subset: str, used_goals: set[str] | None = None,
261	) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
262	    """生成一个任务组（E/I/N 三版共享 goal/DAG/约束集）。
263	
264	    约束驱动构造：先采约束类型，再把支撑角色注入 DAG（保证五类均衡且支持度成立）。
265	    v3 修复：goal 全局唯一（used_goals 跨 split 共享）。goal 唯一 => N 版 query 唯一，
266	    且 E/I query 以 goal 为前缀 => 全部 query 全局唯一（C-LEAK-1 根治）。
267	    """
268	    # 池选择：tpl_ho 用 test 模板池；tool_ho 用 held-out 角色；其余 train
269	    tpl_pool = "test" if subset == "test_tpl_ho" else "train"
270	    dag_pool = HELDOUT_ROLE_POOL if subset == "test_tool_ho" else TRAIN_ROLE_POOL
271	    if used_goals is None:
272	        used_goals = set()
273	    # tool_ho 子集无 tool_auth 配对（held-out 无授权惯例对），如实降级
274	    type_menu = [t for t in CONSTRAINT_TYPES if not (subset == "test_tool_ho" and t == "tool_auth")]
275	
276	    for _attempt in range(30):
277	        # 1) 约束类型：五类均衡采 1-3 条
278	        n_const = rng.choices([1, 2, 3], weights=[0.4, 0.4, 0.2])[0]
279	        chosen_types = rng.sample(type_menu, min(n_const, len(type_menu)))
280	        # 2) 注入支撑角色（顺序即层序，pair 的 before/approval 必须排前）
281	        pinned: list[str] = []
282	        pair_hints: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
283	
284	        def pin(role: str) -> None:
285	            if role not in pinned:
286	                pinned.append(role)
287	
288	        for ctype in chosen_types:
289	            if ctype == "budget":
290	                # tool_ho 的 DAG 必须全 held-out 角色：用 FL 算力配额角色支撑 budget
291	                inject = ["create_fl_round"] if subset == "test_tool_ho" else BUDGET_INJECT_ROLES
292	                pin(rng.choice(inject))
293	            elif ctype == "tool_auth":
294	                pair = rng.choice(AUTH_PAIRS)
295	                pin(pair[0]); pin(pair[1])
296	                pair_hints.append(pair)
297	            elif ctype == "order":
298	                pool_pairs = [p for p in ORDER_PAIRS if all(r in dag_pool for r in p)]
299	                if not pool_pairs:
300	                    chosen_types = [t for t in chosen_types if t != "order"]
301	                    continue
302	                pair = rng.choice(pool_pairs)
303	                pin(pair[0]); pin(pair[1])
304	                pair_hints.append(pair)
305	        if not chosen_types:
306	            continue
307	        # pair 顺序重排：保证每个 hint 的 before 位于 after 前
308	        for before, after in pair_hints:
309	            if pinned.index(before) > pinned.index(after):
310	                pinned.remove(before)
311	                pinned.insert(pinned.index(after), before)
312	        # 3) 补随机角色到 3-6 个
313	        n_dag = rng.randint(max(3, len(pinned)), 6)
314	        filler = [r for r in rng.sample(dag_pool, len(dag_pool)) if r not in pinned]
315	        dag_roles = pinned + filler[: max(0, n_dag - len(pinned))]
316	        graph = build_dag(rng, list(dag_roles))
317	        pii_class = rng.choice(list(PII_CLASSES)) if rng.random() < 0.85 else None
318	        assign_attributes(rng, graph, pii_class)
319	        # 4) 目录：DAG 角色 + 干扰角色；privacy 被选时强制含 external 候选
320	        n_catalog = rng.randint(10, 16)
321	        distractors = [r for r in rng.sample(ALL_ROLE_POOL, len(ALL_ROLE_POOL)) if r not in dag_roles]
322	        if "privacy" in chosen_types:
323	            ext_extra = [r for r in distractors if r in EXTERNAL_ROLES]
324	            if not any(r in EXTERNAL_ROLES for r in dag_roles) and ext_extra:
325	                distractors.remove(ext_extra[0])
326	                distractors.insert(0, ext_extra[0])
327	        catalog = sorted(set(dag_roles) | set(distractors[: max(0, n_catalog - len(dag_roles))]))
328	        # 5) 生成约束（chosen_types 逐一尝试；失败的类型丢弃）
329	        constraints = []
330	        for ctype in chosen_types:
331	            c = make_constraint(rng, ctype, graph, catalog, pii_class)
332	            if c is not None:
333	                constraints.append(c)
334	        if not constraints:
335	            continue
336	        # goal 渲染（全局唯一：重采至不与 used_goals 撞；池子 20x30x12=7200 足够）
337	        goal = None
338	        for _g_attempt in range(80):
339	            cand = fill_template(
340	                GOAL_TEMPLATES[tpl_pool][rng.randrange(len(GOAL_TEMPLATES[tpl_pool]))],
341	                {"dataset": rng.choice(DATASETS), "team": rng.choice(TEAMS)},
342	            )
343	            if cand not in used_goals:
344	                goal = cand
345	                break
346	        if goal is None:
347	            return None
348	        available_roles = sorted(f"role:{r}" for r in catalog)
349	        tool_catalog = [
350	            {"role": r, "category": ROLES[r][1], "subsystem": ROLES[r][0]} for r in catalog
351	        ]
352	        # witness：拓扑序执行模拟
353	        witness = [
354	            {
355	                "step": i, "role": n["role"], "cost_cny": n["cost_cny"],
356	                "duration_min": n["duration_min"], "recipient": n["recipient"],
357	                "data_classes": list(n["data_classes"]),
358	            }
359	            for i, n in enumerate(topo_order(graph))
360	        ]
361	        records = []
362	        for variant in VARIANTS:
363	            if variant == "none":
364	                query = goal
365	                gold_constraints = []
366	                template_ids, hint_meta = [], []
367	            else:
368	                sentences, meta = render_sentences(rng, constraints, variant, tpl_pool)
369	                query = goal + " " + " ".join(sentences) if sentences else goal
370	                template_ids = [m["template_id"] for m in meta]
371	                hint_meta = [
372	                    {k: m[k] for k in ("hint_type", "difficulty")} for m in meta
373	                ]
374	                gold_constraints = []
375	                for c, m, sent in zip(constraints, meta, sentences):
376	                    gc = {k: v for k, v in c.items() if not k.startswith("_")}
377	                    gc["state"] = variant
378	                    gc["evidence_span"] = sent
379	                    gold_constraints.append(gc)
380	            if variant != "none" and not gold_constraints:
381	                continue
382	            record = {
383	                "sample_id": f"{group_id}-{variant[0].upper()}",
384	                "group_id": group_id,
385	                "split": "train" if subset == "train" else "dev" if subset == "dev" else "test",
386	                "subset": subset,
387	                "variant": variant,
388	                "template_ids": template_ids,
389	                "hint_meta": hint_meta,
390	                "task_goal": goal,
391	                "query": query,
392	                "available_roles": available_roles,
393	                "tool_catalog": tool_catalog,
394	                "graph": {
395	                    "nodes": [
396	                        {k: v for k, v in n.items()} for n in graph["nodes"]
397	                    ],
398	                    "edges": graph["edges"],
399	                },
400	                "witness": witness,
401	                "gold": {
402	                    "query_state": variant,
403	                    "abstain": False,
404	                    "constraints": gold_constraints,
405	                },
406	            }
407	            records.append(record)
408	        if len(records) == 3:
409	            return {"group_id": group_id, "subset": subset, "records": records}
410	    return None
411	
412	
413	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 主流程
414	def main() -> None:
415	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
416	    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path, default=ROOT / "configs" / "dataset_v2.yaml")
417	    args = parser.parse_args()
418	    import yaml  # 延迟导入，保持生成器无 yaml 依赖也可被测试
419	
420	    cfg = yaml.safe_load(args.config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
421	    seed = cfg["seed"]
422	    counts = cfg["groups"]  # {train, dev, test_tpl_ho, test_tool_ho}
423	    out_dir = ROOT / cfg["output_dir"]
424	    rng = random.Random(seed)
425	
426	    all_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
427	    groups_by_subset: dict[str, int] = Counter()
428	    used_goals: set[str] = set()  # 全局 goal 唯一性（跨 split 共享；C-LEAK-1 修复）
429	    failures = 0
430	    for subset, n in counts.items():
431	        made = 0
432	        idx = 0
433	        while made < n:
434	            group_id = f"{subset}-{idx:05d}"
435	            group = gen_group(rng, group_id, subset, used_goals)
436	            idx += 1
437	            if group is None:
438	                failures += 1
439	                if failures > 200:
440	                    raise SystemExit("生成失败次数过多，请检查支持度配置")
441	                continue
442	            used_goals.add(group["records"][0]["task_goal"])
443	            all_rows.extend(group["records"])
444	            groups_by_subset[subset] += 1
445	            made += 1
446	
447	    # 写盘
448	    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
449	    files: dict[str, Path] = {}
450	    for subset in counts:
451	        rows = [r for r in all_rows if r["subset"] == subset]
452	        path = out_dir / f"{subset}.jsonl"
453	        path.write_text(
454	            "".join(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True) + "\n" for r in rows),
455	            encoding="utf-8",
456	        )
457	        files[subset] = path
458	
459	    # QC 统计（S8 初版；完整复查由 verify_dataset_v2.py 执行）
460	    def subset_rows(name: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
461	        return [r for r in all_rows if r["subset"] == name]
462	
463	    type_dist = Counter(
464	        c["type"] for r in all_rows for c in r["gold"]["constraints"]
465	    )
466	    hint_dist = Counter(
467	        (m["hint_type"], m["difficulty"])
468	        for r in all_rows if r["variant"] == "implicit" for m in r["hint_meta"]
469	    )
470	    report = {
471	        "dataset": "consdag_trusted_constraint_dataset_v2",
472	        "synthetic_only": True,
473	        "seed": seed,
474	        "groups": dict(groups_by_subset),
475	        "records": {k: len(subset_rows(k)) for k in counts},
476	        "constraint_type_distribution": dict(type_dist),
477	        "implicit_hint_distribution": {f"{h}-d{d}": n for (h, d), n in sorted(hint_dist.items())},
478	        "constraint_count_per_group": dict(Counter(
479	            len([r for r in all_rows if r["variant"] != "none" and r["group_id"] == g][0]["gold"]["constraints"])
480	            for g in {r["group_id"] for r in all_rows}
481	        )),
482	        "generation_failures": failures,
483	        "sha256": {
484	            k: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for k, p in files.items()
485	        },
486	        "limitations": [
487	            "Synthetic, hand-templated corpus; not naturalistic user language.",
488	            "Oracle recoverability check (S6) not yet run; PE oracle pending API key.",
489	            "All gold confidence values are construction-time 1.0; no calibration target.",
490	            "No ambiguous or abstention-required examples by design (implicit red line).",
491	            "test_tool_ho subset contains no tool_auth constraints (no held-out auth pairs).",
492	        ],
493	    }
494	    (out_dir / "generation_report.json").write_text(
495	        json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
496	    )
497	    print(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
498	
499	
500	if __name__ == "__main__":
501	    main()
502

[\"@acquire\"]:\n            out = out[:1] + [role] + out[1:]\n            continue\n        present = [t for t in targets if t in out]\n        if present:\n            out = _insert_before(out, role, min(present, key=out.index))\n    return out\n"

  "content": "\"\"\"dataset_v4 独立验证器（发布包泄漏/可行性测试）。任何硬门槛失败 => verdict FAIL，非零退出。\n\nV1 schema；V2 witness 计划经独立检查器完成目标且满足全部金标约束；\nV3 咬合：默认计划违反每条金标约束；V4 必要性：去掉 c 后的最小改动计划违反 c；\nV5 三元组：同组同任务同 goal、句槽数相同、E/I 金标约束（除 state/evidence）一致、N 金标为空、\n   E/I/N 只在约束句槽上不同；V6 证据：evidence_span 是 query 子串，E 版句含参数原值，\n   I 版句无指令词，budget/deadline 的 I 版 d2/d3 句不含金标数值；\nV7 泄漏：跨 split query/goal/group 零重叠；held-out 工具名不出现在非 tool_ho 记录的任何输入中；\n   test 池模板 id 不出现在 train/dev；V8 文本质量：无相邻重复词；\nV9 下游刻度：无约束规划在 E/I 上安全成功率为 0、在 N 上为 1；金标规划处处为 1。\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport re\nimport sys\nfrom collections import defaultdict\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nHERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nsys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))\n\nfrom dataset_v4_spec import DIRECTIVE_LEXICON, HELDOUT_ROLES, tool_name  # noqa: E402\nfrom trust_env import check, plan  # noqa: E402\n\nSUBSETS = [\"train\", \"dev\", \"test_tpl_ho\", \"test_tool_ho\"]\nREPEAT = re.compile(r\"\\b(\\w+) \\1\\b\", re.IGNORECASE)\n\n\ndef load(data_dir: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    return [json.loads(line) for s in SUBSETS\n            for line in (data_dir / f\"{s}.jsonl\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines() if line.strip()]\n\n\ndef model_input(row: dict[str, Any]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"编译器能看到的全部输入（query + 目录）。\"\"\"\n    return row[\"query\"] + \" \" + json.dumps(row[\"catalog\"], ensure_ascii=False)\n\n\ndef core(c: dict[str, Any]) -> str:\n    return json.dumps({k: c[k] for k in (\"type\", \"severity\", \"scope\", \"params\")}, sort_keys=True)\n\n\ndef verify(rows: list[dict[str, Any]], necessity_sample: int | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    errors: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)\n    groups: dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(dict)\n    for r in rows:\n        groups[r[\"group_id\"]][r[\"variant\"]] = r\n\n    for gi, (gid, g) in enumerate(sorted(groups.items())):\n        if set(g) != {\"explicit\", \"implicit\", \"none\"}:\n            errors[\"V5_triplet\"].append(gid)\n            continue\n        e, i, n = g[\"explicit\"], g[\"implicit\"], g[\"none\"]\n        task = e[\"task\"]\n        gold = e[\"gold\"][\"constraints\"]\n        # V1\n        for r in (e, i, n):\n            if r[\"gold\"][\"query_state\"] != r[\"variant\"] or not isinstance(r[\"gold\"][\"constraints\"], list):\n                errors[\"V1_schema\"].append(r[\"sample_id\"])\n        # V5\n        same = all(r[\"task\"] == task and r[\"task_goal\"] == e[\"task_goal\"] for r in (i, n))\n        slots = len(e[\"template_ids\"]) == len(i[\"template_ids\"]) == len(n[\"template_ids\"])\n        if not (same and slots and not n[\"gold\"][\"constraints\"] and [core(c) for c in gold] == [core(c) for c in i[\"gold\"][\"constraints\"]]):\n            errors[\"V5_triplet\"].append(gid)\n        diff = [k for k, (a, b, c) in enumerate(zip(e[\"template_ids\"], i[\"template_ids\"], n[\"template_ids\"])) if not (a == b == c)]\n        if len(diff) != len(gold):\n            errors[\"V5_minimal_pair\"].append(gid)\n        # V2-V4\n        if not check(task, e[\"witness_plan\"], gold)[\"safe_success\"]:\n            errors[\"V2_witness\"].append(gid)\n        if not all(check(task, e[\"default_plan\"], [c])[\"violations\"] for c in gold):\n            errors[\"V3_binding\"].append(gid)\n        if necessity_sample is None or gi % max(1, len(groups) // necessity_sample) == 0:\n            for k, c in enumerate(gold):\n                relaxed, _ = plan(task, gold[:k] + gold[k + 1:])\n                if relaxed is None or not check(task, relaxed, [c])[\"violations\"]:\n                    errors[\"V4_necessity\"].append(gid)\n                    break\n        # V6\n        for r in (e, i):\n            for c, meta in zip(r[\"gold\"][\"constraints\"], r[\"hint_meta\"] or [{}] * len(r[\"gold\"][\"constraints\"])):\n                span = c[\"evidence_span\"]\n                if span not in r[\"query\"]:\n                    errors[\"V6_span\"].append(r[\"sample_id\"])\n                if r[\"variant\"] == \"explicit\" and not explicit_mentions(c, span):\n                    errors[\"V6_explicit_value\"].append(r[\"sample_id\"])\n                if r[\"variant\"] == \"implicit\":\n                    low = \" \" + span.lower()\n                    if any(w in low for w in DIRECTIVE_LEXICON):\n                        errors[\"V6_implicit_directive\"].append(r[\"sample_id\"])\n                    value = numeric_value(c)\n                    if value is not None and meta.get(\"difficulty\", 1) >= 2 and re.search(rf\"\\b{re.escape(value)}\\b\", span):\n                        errors[\"V6_implicit_value_leak\"].append(r[\"sample_id\"])\n        # V8\n        for r in (e, i, n):\n            if REPEAT.search(r[\"query\"]):\n                errors[\"V8_repeat_word\"].append(r[\"sample_id\"])\n        # V9\n        none_plan, _ = plan(task, [])\n        gold_plan, _ = plan(task, gold)\n        if check(task, none_plan, gold)[\"safe_success\"] or not check(task, gold_plan, gold)[\"safe_success\"]:\n            errors[\"V9_exec_scale\"].append(gid)\n\n    # V7\n    by_subset: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(list)\n    for r in rows:\n        by_subset[r[\"subset\"]].append(r)\n    leak = {}\n    for key in (\"query\", \"task_goal\", \"group_id\"):\n        train_vals = {r[key] for r in by_subset[\"train\"]}\n        for s in SUBSETS[1:]:\n            overlap = len({r[key] for r in by_subset[s]} & train_vals)\n            leak[f\"{s}_{key}_overlap_with_train\"] = overlap\n            if overlap:\n                errors[\"V7_cross_split\"].append(f\"{s}:{key}:{overlap}\")\n    heldout_tokens = HELDOUT_ROLES + [tool_name(r) for r in HELDOUT_ROLES]\n    for r in rows:\n        if r[\"subset\"] != \"test_tool_ho\":\n            text = model_input(r)\n            if any(t in text for t in heldout_tokens):\n                errors[\"V7_heldout_tool_seen\"].append(r[\"sample_id\"])\n    for r in by_subset[\"train\"] + by_subset[\"dev\"]:\n        if any(t.startswith(\"test:\") for t in r[\"template_ids\"]):\n            errors[\"V7_template_pool\"].append(r[\"sample_id\"])\n\n    hard = {k: len(v) for k, v in errors.items()}\n    return {\n        \"records\": len(rows),\n        \"groups\": len(groups),\n        \"failures\": hard,\n        \"leakage\": leak,\n        \"sample_errors\": {k: v[:5] for k, v in errors.items()},\n        \"verdict\": \"PASS\" if not hard else \"FAIL\",\n    }\n\n\ndef numeric_value(c: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:\n    p = c[\"params\"]\n    if c[\"type\"] == \"budget\":\n        return f\"{p['max_total_cost_cny']:,}\"\n    if c[\"type\"] == \"deadline\":\n        return str(p[\"max_duration_hours\"])\n    return None\n\n\ndef explicit_mentions(c: dict[str, Any], span: str) -> bool:\n    p = c[\"params\"]\n    low = span.lower()\n    if c[\"type\"] in (\"budget\", \"deadline\"):\n        return numeric_value(c) in span\n    if c[\"type\"] == \"privacy\":\n        return True  # 数据类可读名由模板直填，见 V5 core 一致性\n    keys = (\"approval_role\", \"required_role\") if c[\"type\"] == \"tool_auth\" else (\"before_role\", \"after_role\")\n    return all(tool_name(p[k]).lower() in low for k in keys)\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    parser.add_argument(\"--data-dir\", type=Path, default=HERE.parent / \"data\" / \"processed_v4\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--necessity-sample\", type=int, default=None,\n                        help=\"只对约 N 个组复核必要性（默认全量）\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    report = verify(load(args.data_dir), args.necessity_sample)\n    (args.data_dir / \"verification_report.json\").write_text(\n        json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + \"\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    print(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))\n    if report[\"verdict\"] != \"PASS\":\n        sys.exit(1)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

12	def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
13	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
14	    with path.open("rb") as stream:
15	        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
16	            digest.update(chunk)
17	    return digest.hexdigest()
18

20	def recompute(data_dir: Path, prediction_dir: Path, model: str, seed: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
21	    result: dict[str, Any] = {
22	        "metrics_version": "e1_score_v4",
23	        "model": model,
24	        "seed": seed,
25	        "source": "saved raw predictions scored by src/run_e1.py",
26	        "subsets": {},
27	    }
28	    for subset in SUBSETS:
29	        data_path = data_dir / f"{subset}.jsonl"
30	        prediction_path = prediction_dir / f"{subset}.jsonl"
31	        rows = load_jsonl(data_path)
32	        records = load_jsonl(prediction_path)
33	        by_id = {record["sample_id"]: record for record in records}
34	        if len(by_id) != len(records):
35	            raise ValueError(f"duplicate prediction sample_id in {prediction_path}")
36	        expected_ids = {row["sample_id"] for row in rows}
37	        if expected_ids != set(by_id):
38	            raise ValueError(
39	                f"sample_id mismatch for {subset}: missing={len(expected_ids - set(by_id))}, "
40	                f"extra={len(set(by_id) - expected_ids)}"
41	            )
42	        predictions = [by_id[row["sample_id"]]["prediction"] for row in rows]
43	        raw = [by_id[row["sample_id"]].get("raw", "") for row in rows]
44	        result["subsets"][subset] = score(rows, predictions, raw)
45	        result["subsets"][subset]["data_sha256"] = sha256(data_path)
46	        result["subsets"][subset]["prediction_sha256"] = sha256(prediction_path)
47	    return result

53	    parser.add_argument("--prediction-dir", type=Path, required=True)
54	    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)

56	    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)

Here are the main 2026 arXiv papers I found on implicit or extracted constraints in LLM agent tool planning:

**Closest to implicit constraints in user requests**

- **LogiSafetyBench (arXiv 2601.08196)**: This one fits your query most directly. It calls itself the first evaluation suite designed to rigorously measure implicit regulatory compliance in LLM tool calling. Its "safety masking" step converts these traces into natural language instructions that omit mandatory safety steps, forcing LLMs to infer implicit constraints from context. The authors found that although scaling improves general reasoning ability, it does not resolve failures in implicit regulatory compliance.
- **AdaPlanBench (arXiv 2606.05622)**: A dynamic and interactive benchmark evaluating LLM's adaptive planning ability under world and user constraints. In this benchmark, world constraints capture tool availability and usability in the environment, whereas user constraints capture whether the tools used in a plan, or the attributes implied by their use, align with user preferences. Its tasks are built by a multi-agent pipeline whose agents handle query rewriting and filtering, candidate plan proposal, constraint extraction, and constraint aggregation and validation.
- **CARL: Constraint-Aware RL for Planning (arXiv 2607.04854)**: The appendix includes the prompt designed to extract implicit constraints in T-Eval and a sensitivity analysis of the extraction quality.

**Implicit sub-goals and dependency extraction**

- **PlanBench-XL (arXiv 2606.22388)**: An interactive benchmark of 327 retail tasks over 1,665 tools. It requires agents to infer implicit sub-goals and discover useful tool-use paths.
- **PeakBench (arXiv 2608.24509)**: Its first evaluation dimension tests whether the model can recover the intrinsic data-flow constraints of a multi-tool workflow before physical execution. The main result is that strong logical planning does not reliably translate into safe or efficient execution under resource constraints.

**Related constraint-focused benchmarks**

- **DisasterBench (arXiv 2605.27957)**: Planning over tools with typed interface constraints, where tool mismatch and parameter-binding errors dominate.
- **SCHEDBench (arXiv 2608.00991)**: Tests how faithfully LLMs follow constraints in natural-language combinatorial scheduling.
- **ATLAS (arXiv 2509.25586, from 2025)**: An earlier travel-planning approach where a Constraint Manager agent extracts explicit constraints and uses commonsense to infer the crucial implicit constraints that are necessary for creating a coherent and logical plan.

If you only read two, I'd pick LogiSafetyBench and AdaPlanBench.

I didn't find a single paper that directly compares a fine-tuned small model doing structured constraint extraction against a prompted GPT model for agent safety-policy compliance. Several 2025–2026 arXiv papers cover parts of that question:

**Large models extract policies, small models enforce them**
- **Policy-as-Prompt (arXiv 2509.23994):** The authors found that while large proprietary models excel in policy extraction, smaller models can still effectively enforce policies with curated prompts. They also say prompting effort was greater for GPT-family models, potentially biasing results and limiting apples-to-apples comparisons.

**Fine-tuned moderation vs. GPT-based reasoning**
- **PAM: Training Policy-Aligned Moderation Filters at Scale (arXiv 2505.19766, COLM 2026):** This is a framework that compiles natural language policies into structured supervision. It compares a fine-tuned variant (PAM-FT), CoT-based variants and a probing approach. The probing approach is reported as over 100× faster than gpt-oss-safeguard, and the authors conclude that structured, policy-aligned supervision is most effectively realized through a lightweight probing model.

**Breaking regulations into atomic constraints for tool use**
- **LogiSafetyGen / LogiSafetyBench (arXiv 2601.08196):** The authors leverage LLMs to distill regulations into atomic constraints, and they use GPT-5-Mini as the backbone engine for policy extraction and instruction synthesis. They found that SOTA LLMs lack the autonomy to infer implicit safety constraints, frequently prioritizing functional success over regulatory adherence.

**Formal policy-as-code instead of probabilistic guardrails**
- **Autoformalization of Agent Instructions into Policy-as-Code (arXiv 2606.26649):** This paper argues that most current approaches rely on probabilistic guardrails (fine-tuned classifiers, prompt-based steering) that offer no formal guarantees. As an alternative, it translates prompts, MCP tool descriptions and policy documents into formally verified Cedar policies using an LLM-based generator-critic loop.

**Model size in policy compliance reasoning**
- **Knowledge Graph Representations for LLM-Based Policy Compliance Reasoning (arXiv 2604.27713):** The authors tested models from gpt-5-mini down to a 3B granite model. They report that agentic graph traversal degrades performance for smaller models.

**Effect of safety fine-tuning on agent compliance**
- **Why Do AI Agents Break Rules? (arXiv 2608.12323):** This paper shows that safety-fine-tuned models maintain compliance broadly, while task-optimized and agentic models treat regulatory signals as mere optimization parameters.

**Other related work**
- **LCO (arXiv 2605.27375):** This paper uses LLM-generated safety constraints to make agents safer on real-world tasks.
- **Chance-Constrained LLM Fine-tuning (arXiv 2609.29960):** This paper treats keeping a model safe during fine-tuning as a reliability constraint rather than an auxiliary objective.

I can run narrower searches if you want, for example "distilled constraint extractor" or "SLM vs GPT-4o policy extraction".

The search turned up several 2026 papers on this. Each one covers part of your query, but none puts GRPO, privacy authorization and violation penalties in a single benchmark.

**1. Least-privilege tool selection trained with GRPO** (arXiv 2606.20023, "When Lower Privileges Suffice")
- This is the closest match to "violation penalty + reward shaping." The authors first do supervised fine-tuning on privilege-aware trajectories, then optimize the policy with GRPO (Shao et al., 2024) in the simulated multi-turn tool-use environment.
- In the reward, successful completion with standard tools is preferred, escalation is acceptable only after meaningful low-privilege exploration, and premature risk-tool use is penalized most strongly when it occurs without prior standard-tool attempts. Failed trajectories may still receive partial credit if they explore standard tools without unnecessary escalation.

**2. ToolPrivacyBench** (arXiv 2606.28061): a privacy and authorization benchmark
- It audits whether task-private atoms are routed only to authorized tools and downstream sinks, thereby evaluating both task completion and privacy over-disclosure during tool use.
- It contains 2,150 cases, including 1,150 fully synthetic privacy-sensitive business workflows and 1,000 cases adapted from existing multi-tool and function-calling benchmarks. Each policy knowledge base is projected into a field-tool authorization matrix.
- Main finding: successful tool execution does not imply appropriate privacy disclosure: an agent may complete a task while transmitting unnecessary private information through intermediate tool calls.
- It's an evaluation benchmark, not an RL training method. Its authorization matrix could serve as a source for a violation-penalty reward.

**3. SiLR** (arXiv 2609.04629): process rewards built from constraint violations
- The paper argues that counting violations gives GRPO a weak signal: With B concurrent violation branches, a count-based reward takes at most B+1 distinct values. As a result, action pairs within a count-equivalence class therefore receive identical immediate reward and have no step-level advantage separation.
- Its "geometric" violation reward converges to full recovery within five GRPO iterations; the count reward—blind to the drift its own actions cause—is driven below its random initialization.

**4. PROBE** (arXiv 2610.22124): GRPO used to find policy violations
- This flips the setup: GRPO trains an auditor that hunts for violations in other agents. The authors formalize agent auditing as a two-player Markov game and propose a composite reward that balances violation discovery, behavioral plausibility, conversation progress, and policy diversity.
- They report that GRPO and GFlowNet are reward-scale sensitive: in representative checkpoints, calibration raises their training-time yields by 63% and 78%, respectively.

**5. Background**
- MDP-GRPO was evaluated on FollowBench, IFEval, and a curated multi-constraint dataset, where it outperformed standard GRPO in strict constraint satisfaction while maintaining general capabilities. This is general constraint following, not tool authorization.
- A 2026 survey of RL post-training for tool agents covers GRPO's KL penalty, DAPO refinements and how reward hacking happens (zylos.ai).

If you want a training recipe, start with paper #1's reward design. Borrow the authorization labels from #2 and the advice on dense, non-count violation rewards from #3.

Sources:
- [When Lower Privileges Suffice (arXiv 2606.20023)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.20023)
- [ToolPrivacyBench (arXiv 2606.28061)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28061)

为准。\n\n---\n\n## 3. 创新点口径（收窄后，能立住的版本）\n\n- **①**：一个**可训练、planner-agnostic、输出可审计**的约束编译器，输出 typed 约束对象（type/params/state/severity/scope/evidence_span）。主张落在\"同一信息条件下，小模型训练后的编译质量和下游执行级安全成功率，不低于（或优于）强模型 PE，并且可本机部署\"。\n  - **不得**声称训练编译器、evidence span、隐式约束、拒判是\"零先例\"。\n  - **校准/拒判在 v4 中不主张**：gold confidence 已删除；E5 改为用序列对数概率做 selective risk 的事后分析，且需要单独构造歧义集（§4.4）。\n- **②**：只有在 E2 跑出\"外部锚、节点归因、非对称罚各自有独立增益\"之后才能写成贡献。在那之前只写成方法设计。\n- **③**：主张\"**咬合 + 逐条必要的约束集 + E/I/N 最小三元组 + 双 held-out + 执行级刻度**\"这个组合。**禁写\"三版语义等价\"**，改写为\"(E, I) 等价对 + N 对比臂\"。\n- 首创句式沿用蓝本 §1.5 的模板，并必须附检索协议（日期、库、查询式），把 LogiSafetyBench、AM-Bench、ExecutionFirst、LIFT 加进划界表。\n\n---\n\n## 4. 数据集 v4（已实现、已验证）\n\n### 4.1 v3 → v4 变更\n\n| 维度 | v3 | v4 |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| 任务世界 | 单一 DAG = 唯一计划 | 5 个阶段、每阶段 1–3 个备选工具（费用/时长/本地或外发/是否清除 PII），可插入审批、脱敏、校验步骤，finish 两步顺序可交换 |\n| 约束咬合 | 0%（全部被默认计划满足） | **100%**：默认计划违反每条金标约束（V3）；**逐条必要**：去掉 c 后的最小改动计划必违反 c（V4，5000 组全量复核） |\n| N 版 | = goal 原句 | 同一句槽换成**同主题近似干扰句**（豁免、否定、他人适用、已撤销）；40% 的组另带一条三版共享的干扰槽 |\n| I 版 | 指令改写 | 无指令词（词边界正则，V6）；budget/deadline 的 d2/d3 需要减法或加法，金标数值不出现在句中（含\"1,350 含 350\"这类尾数捷径，V6）；privacy 的 d2/d3 只给字段名，要按策略卡映射到数据类 |\n| held-out 工具 | 训练目录里出现 held-out 名 | held-out 世界 22 个工具名**从未出现**在 train/dev/tpl_ho 的任何模型输入中（V7） |\n| 契约公平性 | severity/scope 是隐藏约定 | 策略卡随 prompt 给出类型、参数键、severity、scope 规则和 state 定义；删掉恒定的 confidence/description |\n| 规模 | 5000 组 × 3 | 相同：train 4000 / dev 300 / tpl_ho 350 / tool_ho 350 组（15,000 条） |\n| 分布 | — | 约束数 1/2/3 = 2665/1844/491；类型：order 2058、privacy 1764、tool_auth 1563、deadline 1352、budget 1089；I 难度 d1/d2/d3 = 2326/3139/2306（按 explicit 版统计，生成报告） |\n\n验证门槛 V1–V9（`src/verify_dataset_v4.py`）全部 PASS，跨 split 的 query/goal/group 重叠为 0。\nSHA256（LF）：train `eaabe109…`、dev `e7ff77f1…`、test_tpl_ho `04de746c…`、test_tool_ho `23e8b9b6…`。服务器重新生成后哈希逐一相同。\n\n### 4.2 执行级刻度（E1-exec，`src/eval_exec.py`）\n\n编译输出经严格解析后交给**最小改动约束感知规划器**（代表完美服从约束的 planner），产出计划，再由**独立检查器**用金标约束判定 safe_success（完成目标且零违反）。\n\n- 刻度两端：none 档在 E/I 上为 0、在 N 上为 1；gold 档处处为 1。\n- 附带指标：逐类型违反率；N 版的不必要偏离率；E/I 版安全时的过度改动率；group bootstrap 95% CI；两系统间做配对 bootstrap + 精确 McNemar。\n\n这一项回答了\"F1 高是否有用\"，也让对不同契约表述宽容的指标（核心键 type+params）有了执行意义。\n\n### 4.3 仍有的局限（如实写进 limitations）\n\n- 纯模板合成；held-out 世界与训练世界**结构同构**，只是名字和属性没见过。\n- 规划器是符号的最小改动规划器，不是 LLM planner。E6 再换 LLM planner。\n\n### 4.4 数据侧待补（P0/P1）\n\n| 优先级 | 内容 | 做法 | 依赖 |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| P0 | I 版可恢复性 oracle | ≥2 家强模型零样本恢复约束，**看不到 gold**；恢复集 = 金标（type+params）才准入；N 版须恢复出空集；按类型和难度报一致率 | 有效 API（Claude/Codex 中转可用；qwen-max 的 key 要复核） |\n| P0 | 人工盲审 | 2–3 人，每类型 ≥50 条，共 ≥250 条；按\"可恢复 / 唯一 / 自然 / N 无约束\"四维打分；报 Krippendorff α 或 Gwet AC1 | 标注人 |\n| P1 | 改写 OOD 子集 | 强模型改写 300 组 tpl_ho，**约束保持门**用 gold 规划器加检查器复核（LIFT 的教训：改写模型可能\"执行\"约束），人工抽审 | API |\n| P1 | 外部 OOD | ToolPrivacyBench 或 τ²-bench 的子集映射到我们的 schema，作为零训练迁移评测 | 获取数据 |\n| P2 | 歧义档 A | 对接 AM-Bench：线索不足以唯一确定参数，gold = abstain，用于 E5 | 设计 gold 语义 |\n\n---\n\n## 5. 实验设计（v4）\n\n### 5.1 E1 主表（编译器）：同服务器、同代码、同依赖、bf16、seed 42\n\n| 臂 | 系统 | 状态 |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Z1–Z3 | Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B/4B 零样本（同一 v4 prompt 含策略卡） | **运行中**（队列内） |\n| T1–T3 | 同底座 LoRA（r16/α32/dropout 0.05，lr 2e-4，3 epoch，grad-accum 4，max_seq 1280，completion-only loss） | **运行中**（串行 0.6B→1.7B→4B） |\n| P1–P2 | 强模型 PE（同 prompt，temperature 0）：Claude（relaxycode 中转）/ gpt-6-astra（Codex 中转）/ qwen-max（待 key 复核） | 待跑（CPU/API；可在服务器上跑） |\n| P3 | 强模型 PE + few-shot（每类型 2 例，取自 train） | 待跑 |\n| O | gold 与 none 刻度 | 已内置 |\n\n**指标**：\n- e1_score_v5：严格 F1、核心 F1、state 准确率、记录全对率、N 误报率、逐类型和逐难度、parse rate、malformed 数。\n- e1_exec_v1：safe_success（总体 / 受约束 / 按 variant）、95% CI、逐类型违反率、N 不必要偏离率。\n\n**判胜（预注册）**：\n- T 优于同底座 Z：训练增益。\n- T 对 P：报差值和配对 CI。核心主张压在 **I 档**和 **tool_ho**。\n- 若 T 输给 P，按蓝本 R1 转向\"本机部署 + 成本/延迟\"轴，**照实报告**。\n\n### 5.2 E4 泛化\n\n- dev（in-domain）、tpl_ho（模板、goal、背景、PII 别名全部 held-out）、tool_ho（未见工具世界）分列。\n- 预注册判据：I 档在 tpl_ho 上的下降幅度；tool_ho 的 safe-success。若崩溃，结论改写为\"组合泛化仍是 open problem\"。\n\n### 5.3 E5 校准（降级）\n\n- 用序列平均对数概率做 risk–coverage 曲线、ECE（以 safe_success 为正确性标签）。\n- 不宣称\"学会拒判\"，直到 §4.4 的 A 档补齐。\n\n### 5.4 E6 planner 可移植性\n\n把同一编译输出喂给 ≥3 个 LLM planner（Qwen3-4B/8B、一个异家族模型），用同一检查器判 safe_success。只做推理，可在服务器上跑。\n\n### 5.5 E2/E3（GRPO，阶段 3）：前置条件与设计修正\n\n**前置条件**：v4 的规划世界已经提供独立的成功检查器，以及违反判定（RLVP 式的可验证规则），E2 的信息权限问题由此闭合：\n- C* 只用于离线评测与 ② 的漏检罚。\n- 所有臂拥有相同的信息权限。\n- 训练用 train 世界，评测用 held-out。\n\n**臂（同预算，1.7B LoRA）**：\n- vanilla GRPO\n- ToolRLA 加法（λ=10）\n- GDPO/ScAdv（按分量标准化）\n- TAG 乘性门控（按其探针协议）\n- RLVP 逐动作罚\n- ②完整版\n- ②去门控 / 去归因 / 对称罚\n\n**必报**：\n- 四格（成功 × 满足）、反躺平三联、组内方差可达性预诊断（VarG）。\n- 编译器噪声注入（FP/FN 各 3 档）存活曲线。\n- 3 个 seed 加配对 bootstrap。\n\n**风险**：RLVP 明确写了 \"chain 0.6B/1.7B (too weak)\"。先测 1.7B 的 VarG 和 dead-update 比例，不达标就把 4B（QLoRA）作为主战场。\n\n### 5.6 统计纪律\n\n- 所有比较都在同一测试集上做**配对**检验：group bootstrap 1000 次以上，加精确 McNemar；多重比较做 Holm 校正。\n- 种子：按用户要求主表统一 seed 42。论文里需要注明\"单 seed + 数据层 bootstrap\"。算力允许时，补 0.6B/1.7B 的 seed 43/44，作为训练方差估计。\n- 预注册方向；不支持的结果照报；发散或中止的运行单列计数。\n\n---\n\n## 6. 代码审计结论\n\n| 项 | 结论 |\n| --- | --- |\n| completion-only loss | 正确：prefix 的 label 置 -100，completion 后接 EOS（`train_lora`） |\n| NaN 防护 | 正确：前向 loss 有限性检查、`clip_grad_norm_(error_if_nonfinite=True)`、step 后参数有限性检查、bf16 加载、失败时写 `training_failure.json`。v4 smoke 的首步 loss 为 0.683，数值有限 |\n| 截断丢样 | **已修**：v4 prompt 最长约 1060 token，原 max_seq 1024 会静默丢样本。改为 1280，并打印 dropped 数（smoke 中 12000/12000 保留） |\n| 评分器 | v4 提交了 fail-closed 严格解析；v5 新增核心键（整值浮点按整数处理）、记录全对、N 误报率（显式计数） |\n| 数据可复现 | **已修**：Windows 写盘为 CRLF，导致哈希跨平台不一致。现在显式写 LF，服务器重新生成后哈希相同 |\n| 验证器自身 | v4 单测专门验证它能抓到篡改的 witness、N 版残留约束、held-out 工具泄漏。审计中发现并修正了一次 `\\b` 被 shell 吞掉、导致指令词检查空过的问题 |\n| 测试 | 本地 53 个全部通过（服务器的 conda 环境没有装 pytest；代码同一提交，已在本地跑过） |\n\n---\n\n## 7. 风险与工作量\n\n| 风险 | 触发 | 预案 |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| v4 仍被 0.6B 打满 | dev/tpl_ho/tool_ho 的 safe-success 都 ≥0.99 | 仍有价值（对比 Z/P）。但应补改写 OOD 和外部 OOD，并加大 I 档的推理深度（三事实链） |\n| T 输给强模型 PE | I 档或 tool_ho 上 T < P | 照报；叙事转向成本、延迟、本机部署 |\n| 4B 显存或时间 | OOM 或单模型超过 12h | eval batch 已设为 16；必要时改用梯度检查点 |\n| API 不稳定 | Codex 中转的 SSE 超时 | 断点续跑；Claude 中转作为主 P 臂 |\n\n时间估算（4080S）：每个模型 = zero-shot 评测 + 9000 步 + 训练后评测，0.6B 约 3–4h，1.7B 约 6–8h，4B 约 9–12h，三模型串行约 18–24h。P 臂、oracle、人审与 GPU 队列并行。\n\n---\n\n## 8. 禁止的表述\n\n- 用 v2/v3 或中期报告的任何数字。\n- 拿解析 F1 当执行级安全成功率。\n- 声称\"三版语义等价\"、\"首次 scope 绑定/约束门控\"、\"零先例\"。\n- 说 tool_ho 证明了结构泛化（它只证明了未见名称和属性）。\n- 在 E2 跑出结果之前声称 ② 有下游收益。\n- 声称校准或拒判已经学会。\n"
}

# 结论

1️⃣ **数据集不 ok**，2️⃣ **实验设计也不 ok**。所以我没有直接用 v3 重训，而是先重建数据，再在服务器上重启三模型实验。v4 队列 22:10 已经开跑。

v3 的硬伤（全部在 15,000 条上复算过）：

- **"有没有约束"有捷径可走**：N 版 query 就是 task goal 原句（5000/5000），E/I 版是 goal 后面再加几句（10000/10000），数句子就能判断。
- **约束根本不起约束作用**：17,574 条金标约束全部被唯一的默认计划满足。在 v3 上做执行级评测，"完全不给约束"的基线就能拿 100%。
- **state 测的是措辞风格**：所谓隐式句多是显式改写，例如 "Order of operations here: X, then Y."。0.6B 在 tpl_ho 上的 87 个错误全部是 explicit/implicit 翻转，dev 和 tool_ho 的 strict F1 都是 1.0000。
- **零样本和强模型对照不公平**：severity 由类型硬编码、scope 由图结构推出，这些约定都不在提示里却参与严格匹配。所以零样本和 qwen-max 的 F1≈0 不能拿来证明"训练优于提示"。

v2/v3 的全部数字只作 legacy 诊断，不进任何表。

# 改动清单

- **dataset v4**：
  - 每个阶段有可替换工具，约束 100% 起作用，而且逐条必要（去掉任何一条，规划出的计划必然违反它）。
  - N 版换成同主题的豁免/否定句，句子数与 E/I 版一致。
  - I 版不含指令词，参数需要算出来（如余额减预留、两个时刻相减）。
  - held-out 工具名不出现在任何训练输入里。
  - severity/scope 规则写进提示（策略卡）。
  - 规模不变：15,000 条，train 12000 / dev 900 / 两个 test 各 1050。
  - 9 道验证门槛（V1–V9）全部通过，跨 split 泄漏为 0。
  - 服务器从 GitHub 拉代码后重新生成，数据哈希与本地逐一相同。
- **执行级评测 E1-exec**：编译结果交给规划器出计划，再由独立检查器判"任务完成且零违规"，带 95% CI 和模型间配对检验。刻度两端：不给约束时 E/I 为 0，给金标约束时为 1。
- **评分器 v5**：新增只看 type+params 的核心 F1、整条记录全对率、N 版误报率。
- **代码审计**：completion-only loss 和 NaN 防护（bf16、loss/梯度/参数有限性检查、失败落盘）确认正确。修了三个问题：
  - `max_seq_len` 1024 会静默丢样本，改为 1280；smoke 中 12000 条全保留。
  - Windows 写 CRLF 导致哈希跨平台不一致，改为显式写 LF。
  - 指令词检查的正则曾因 shell 转义失效、测试空过，已修复。
- 本地 53 个测试全部通过。服务器没装 pytest，测试只在本地跑过，代码是同一提交。
- **设计方案** `reports/design_v4_ccfb.md`：
  - 文献范式（四组精读 + 补检索）和三个创新点各自最危险的邻居。
  - 收窄后的主张口径和禁写清单。
  - E1/E4/E5/E6 设计，以及 E2 GRPO 的前置条件和对照臂。
  - 统计纪律、风险与时间估算。
- 实验台账已更新。提交 `5f8fcd6`、`f63c727`、`99f6e84` 均已推送 GitHub。

# 实验命令

服务器目录 `/root/ConsDagQAQ`，代码从 GitHub 浅克隆而来：

```
source /etc/network_turbo && git pull --ff-only origin main
python src/build_dataset_v4.py && python src/verify_dataset_v4.py
nohup bash scripts/run_e1_queue_v4.sh > outputs/e1_v4_queue_master.log 2>&1 &
```

队列串行跑 Qwen3-0.6B → 1.7B → 4B，统一 bf16、seed 42、同一提交。每个模型先跑 2 步 smoke 再跑完整流程，状态写在 `outputs/e1_v4_queue_manifest.jsonl`。

# 当前进度（22:17）

- 旧的 v3 队列已停。当时 1.7B-v3 训练到 5600/9000 步，loss 约 1e-5，结果作废。
- v4 的 0.6B smoke 通过（首步 loss 0.683）。dev 的 zero-shot 已完成（F1 0.010，state 准确率 0.347），正在跑后两个子集，之后进入训练。
- 三个模型全部跑完预计需要 18–24 小时。
- 定时任务 `97a952a5` 每小时第 13、43 分运行，只在本会话内有效，7 天后自动过期。它会：
  - 监控队列，失败时诊断并只重跑失败的模型；
  - 回收每个模型的指标写进台账；
  - GPU 忙时推进强模型 PE 对照、隐式线索可恢复性检查、新文献入库、人工盲审抽样包。

20	1. **N 版捷径**：N 版 query 与 task_goal 完全相同，5000/5000；E/I 版全部是"goal + 额外句"，10000/10000。判断有没有约束，看句子数量就够了。
21	2. **约束不起约束作用**：17,574/17,574 条金标约束已被唯一的 witness/默认计划满足（budget 上限 = 总价 + 余量；deadline 大于总时长；PII 只放本地节点；order/auth 的顺序就是拓扑序）。在 v3 上做执行级评测，无约束基线就是 100%，指标没有区分度。
22	3. **state 由模板池决定，而不是语义**：I 版线索里有 1930/8787 条含指令词或顺序词，例如 "Order of operations here: X, then Y."。tpl_ho 上 87 个错误全部是 explicit/implicit 翻转，说明 state 标签测的是措辞风格。
23	4. **对零样本/PE 不公平**：severity 是 type 的常函数（budget/deadline/privacy=high，tool_auth/order=medium），scope 由图结构确定性推出，confidence 恒为 1.0，但这些约定都不在提示里，却参与严格匹配。所以零样本和 qwen-max 的 F1≈0 主要是契约不可知造成的，不能用来证明"训练优于提示"。
24	5. 附带问题：
25	   - 机械重复文本占 4.7–6.7%。
26	   - 3400/4000 个训练组的目录里出现了 held-out 角色名。
27	   - v3 的 1.7B 在第 5600 步时 loss 已到 1e-5 量级，任务被过度拟合。这次重启时停掉了该运行，结果作废。
28	
29	**v2/v3 的全部 E1 数字只作为 legacy 诊断保留，不进任何表。**
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. 文献范式（4 组精读 + 补充检索）
34	
35	### 2.1 同类工作的实验设计共性
36	
37	- **数据**
38	  - 方法类论文大多复用公开基准（TravelPlanner、τ²-bench、AppWorld 等），测试集几百到一千条。
39	  - 自建基准都带人工或 LLM 审计：PRefine 有 Fleiss κ 0.70/0.88；ANCHOR 五名工程师、Gwet AC1 0.91–0.97；Firefly 用 50+50 盲审加 χ²；ToolTurns 120 条盲审。
40	  - 以训练集为卖点的论文规模在 5k–35k（LIFT 34k，RECAST 30k）。
41	- **基线**：多个强闭源模型 PE、公开方法官方复刻（逐条写明改造点）、结构消融（w/o 编译器、gold 注入、RAW/SELF）。
42	- **指标**：执行级任务成功 + 约束满足 + **联合指标**（safe completion / process-valid / SPR / Verif.&NoDiff / both），再加违规次数和 hacking 诊断。
43	- **统计**：较好的论文用 3–5 个 seed 或 trial，加 10k 次按任务配对 bootstrap，或 Wilson CI / McNemar / Holm 校正。约一半论文没有统计，这是我们可以胜出的地方。
44	- **held-out**：EffectWorld 做了三个 held-out（未见工具和任务类型）；NormWorlds-CF 和 CIRCE 按根族或分组切分。
45	
46	### 2.2 对三个创新点最危险的邻居
47	
48	| 创新点 | 最危险邻居 | 威胁 | 我们必须拿出的差异化证据 |
49	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
50	| ① 训练的证据绑定编译器 | CGAP（零样本 LLM 解析、带字符偏移 evidence span、喂给 PDDL 规划器、执行级加配对统计）；NOMOS / PolicyGuide（"编译器"叙事、typed IR、safe completion）；BeyondReAct（同为 Qwen3 0.6–8B，"小模型编译、强模型执行"） | "为什么不直接 prompt 一个大模型？" | 同 schema、同策略卡下，**强模型 PE 对照**和执行级 safe-success 对比，并按 I 档、tool_ho 分开报告 |
51	| ② 约束锚定奖励分解 | TAG（证明静态权重在 GRPO 下会坍塌，提出乘性锚门控）；RLVP（逐动作罚、折叠标量对比、outcome-gating，原则是 "penalize commission, never omission"）；Constrained GRPO（ScRew 会扭曲非对称比例）；DAGent（GRPO 中的 DAG 节点信用） | g(A) 很容易被看成"TAG 换成外部锚" | 外部锚、节点归因、非对称罚三者**各自独立的增益**；ScAdv/GDPO 对照臂；同预算 TAG 臂 |
52	| ③ E/I/N 配对可执行基准 | AM-Bench（同任务约束的显式/模糊/缺失配对，约束域就是授权和机密数据）；ExecutionFirst（同 DAG 三档显式度，构造期执行验证）；LIFT（合成、配对渲染、训练集、17 个模型）；新检索到的 **LogiSafetyBench 2601.08196**（通过"safety masking"迫使模型推断隐式合规约束）和 **ToolPrivacyBench 2606.28061**（2,150 例隐私授权基准） | "显式/隐式配对已经有人做过" | 我们的 I 版"**可恢复且 gold 唯一**"；有 N 负对照（近似干扰句）；约束**咬合且逐条必要**；双 held-out；带训练用途；执行级刻度 |
53	
54	另外，Implicit Intelligence 定义隐式为 "requirements that users expect but never explicitly state"。按这个定义，我们 I 版的证据仍在 query 里，所以论文里必须把 implicit 定义为**表达状态**（不陈述指令，但可由 query 内事实推出），并引用它来划界。
55	
56	### 2.3 新检索补充（WebSearch；全文暂未入库，WebFetch 被网络策略拦截，**只核实到摘要和搜索结果层面**）
57	
58	- LogiSafetyBench（2601.08196）：隐式法规合规，工具调用，"safety masking"。对③和"隐式"叙事构成**高危**，必须正面引用并对照。
59	- ToolPrivacyBench（2606.28061）：2,150 例，字段–工具授权矩阵，结论是"任务完成 ≠ 隐私合规"。可作为执行级联合指标的直接先例和外部 OOD 评测集候选。
60	- SiLR（2609.04629）：计数型违规奖励在 GRPO 下组内区分度很低。E2 奖励设计要引用。
61	- When Lower Privileges Suffice（2606.20023）：SFT 后接 GRPO，奖励对过早使用高权限工具施罚。是 E2 的近邻。
62	- PeakBench（2608.24509）、PlanBench-XL（2606.22388）：工具规划中的隐式数据流和隐式子目标。
63	- 待办：用 `scripts/fetch_papers.py` 把上述论文拉进 `literature/library` 精读，然后更新划界表。
64	
65	### 2.4 文献库卫生
66	
67	`literature/extracted/papers/` 下有 9 个目录装的是无关论文：ATLAS_2605.16668、CARL_2505.23300、LANG-NCO_2603.07613、RLVP_2510.07896、TAG_2508.09112、ARMA、Hermes、Instructed-Use-Tools、NCP-Benchmark。**一律不得作为证据引用**；以 `literature/extracted/library` 为准。

70	
71	## 3. 创新点口径（收窄后，能立住的版本）
72	
73	- **①**：一个**可训练、planner-agnostic、输出可审计**的约束编译器，输出 typed 约束对象（type/params/state/severity/scope/evidence_span）。主张落在"同一信息条件下，小模型训练后的编译质量和下游执行级安全成功率，不低于（或优于）强模型 PE，并且可本机部署"。
74	  - **不得**声称训练编译器、evidence span、隐式约束、拒判是"零先例"。
75	  - **校准/拒判在 v4 中不主张**：gold confidence 已删除；E5 改为用序列对数概率做 selective risk 的事后分析，且需要单独构造歧义集（§4.4）。
76	- **②**：只有在 E2 跑出"外部锚、节点归因、非对称罚各自有独立增益"之后才能写成贡献。在那之前只写成方法设计。
77	- **③**：主张"**咬合 + 逐条必要的约束集 + E/I/N 最小三元组 + 双 held-out + 执行级刻度**"这个组合。**禁写"三版语义等价"**，改写为"(E, I) 等价对 + N 对比臂"。
78	- 首创句式沿用蓝本 §1.5 的模板，并必须附检索协议（日期、库、查询式），把 LogiSafetyBench、AM-Bench、ExecutionFirst、LIFT 加进划界表。
79	
80	---
81	
82	## 4. 数据集 v4（已实现、已验证）
83	
84	### 4.1 v3 → v4 变更
85	
86	| 维度 | v3 | v4 |
87	| --- | --- | --- |
88	| 任务世界 | 单一 DAG = 唯一计划 | 5 个阶段、每阶段 1–3 个备选工具（费用/时长/本地或外发/是否清除 PII），可插入审批、脱敏、校验步骤，finish 两步顺序可交换 |
89	| 约束咬合 | 0%（全部被默认计划满足） | **100%**：默认计划违反每条金标约束（V3）；**逐条必要**：去掉 c 后的最小改动计划必违反 c（V4，5000 组全量复核） |
90	| N 版 | = goal 原句 | 同一句槽换成**同主题近似干扰句**（豁免、否定、他人适用、已撤销）；40% 的组另带一条三版共享的干扰槽 |
91	| I 版 | 指令改写 | 无指令词（词边界正则，V6）；budget/deadline 的 d2/d3 需要减法或加法，金标数值不出现在句中（含"1,350 含 350"这类尾数捷径，V6）；privacy 的 d2/d3 只给字段名，要按策略卡映射到数据类 |
92	| held-out 工具 | 训练目录里出现 held-out 名 | held-out 世界 22 个工具名**从未出现**在 train/dev/tpl_ho 的任何模型输入中（V7） |
93	| 契约公平性 | severity/scope 是隐藏约定 | 策略卡随 prompt 给出类型、参数键、severity、scope 规则和 state 定义；删掉恒定的 confidence/description |
94	| 规模 | 5000 组 × 3 | 相同：train 4000 / dev 300 / tpl_ho 350 / tool_ho 350 组（15,000 条） |
95	| 分布 | — | 约束数 1/2/3 = 2665/1844/491；类型：order 2058、privacy 1764、tool_auth 1563、deadline 1352、budget 1089；I 难度 d1/d2/d3 = 2387/3073/2366；干扰槽比例 0.407（`generation_report.json`） |
96	
97	验证门槛 V1–V9（`src/verify_dataset_v4.py`）全部 PASS，跨 split 的 query/goal/group 重叠为 0。
98	SHA256（LF）：train `eaabe109…`、dev `e7ff77f1…`、test_tpl_ho `04de746c…`、test_tool_ho `23e8b9b6…`。服务器重新生成后哈希逐一相同。
99	
100	### 4.2 执行级刻度（E1-exec，`src/eval_exec.py`）
101	
102	编译输出经严格解析后交给**最小改动约束感知规划器**（代表完美服从约束的 planner），产出计划，再由**独立检查器**用金标约束判定 safe_success（完成目标且零违反）。
103	
104	- 刻度两端：none 档在 E/I 上为 0、在 N 上为 1；gold 档处处为 1。
105	- 附带指标：逐类型违反率；N 版的不必要偏离率；E/I 版安全时的过度改动率；group bootstrap 95% CI；两系统间做配对 bootstrap + 精确 McNemar。
106	
107	这一项回答了"F1 高是否有用"，也让对不同契约表述宽容的指标（核心键 type+params）有了执行意义。
108	
109	### 4.3 仍有的局限（如实写进 limitations）
110	
111	- 纯模板合成；held-out 世界与训练世界**结构同构**，只是名字和属性没见过。
112	- 规划器是符号的最小改动规划器，不是 LLM planner。E6 再换 LLM planner。
113	
114	### 4.4 数据侧待补（P0/P1）
115	
116	| 优先级 | 内容 | 做法 | 依赖 |
117	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
118	| P0 | I 版可恢复性 oracle | ≥2 家强模型零样本恢复约束，**看不到 gold**；恢复集 = 金标（type+params）才准入；N 版须恢复出空集；按类型和难度报一致率 | 有效 API（Claude/Codex 中转可用；qwen-max 的 key 要复核） |
119	| P0 | 人工盲审 | 2–3 人，每类型 ≥50 条，共 ≥250 条；按"可恢复 / 唯一 / 自然 / N 无约束"四维打分；报 Krippendorff α 或 Gwet AC1 | 标注人 |
120	| P1 | 改写 OOD 子集 | 强模型改写 300 组 tpl_ho，**约束保持门**用 gold 规划器加检查器复核（LIFT 的教训：改写模型可能"执行"约束），人工抽审 | API |
121	| P1 | 外部 OOD | ToolPrivacyBench 或 τ²-bench 的子集映射到我们的 schema，作为零训练迁移评测 | 获取数据 |
122	| P2 | 歧义档 A | 对接 AM-Bench：线索不足以唯一确定参数，gold = abstain，用于 E5 | 设计 gold 语义 |

126	## 5. 实验设计（v4）
127	
128	### 5.1 E1 主表（编译器）：同服务器、同代码、同依赖、bf16、seed 42
129	
130	| 臂 | 系统 | 状态 |
131	| --- | --- | --- |
132	| Z1–Z3 | Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B/4B 零样本（同一 v4 prompt 含策略卡） | **运行中**（队列内） |
133	| T1–T3 | 同底座 LoRA（r16/α32/dropout 0.05，lr 2e-4，3 epoch，grad-accum 4，max_seq 1280，completion-only loss） | **运行中**（串行 0.6B→1.7B→4B） |
134	| P1–P2 | 强模型 PE（同 prompt，temperature 0）：Claude（relaxycode 中转）/ gpt-6-astra（Codex 中转）/ qwen-max（待 key 复核） | 待跑（CPU/API；可在服务器上跑） |
135	| P3 | 强模型 PE + few-shot（每类型 2 例，取自 train） | 待跑 |
136	| O | gold 与 none 刻度 | 已内置 |
137	
138	**指标**：
139	- e1_score_v5：严格 F1、核心 F1、state 准确率、记录全对率、N 误报率、逐类型和逐难度、parse rate、malformed 数。
140	- e1_exec_v1：safe_success（总体 / 受约束 / 按 variant）、95% CI、逐类型违反率、N 不必要偏离率。
141	
142	**判胜（预注册）**：
143	- T 优于同底座 Z：训练增益。
144	- T 对 P：报差值和配对 CI。核心主张压在 **I 档**和 **tool_ho**。
145	- 若 T 输给 P，按蓝本 R1 转向"本机部署 + 成本/延迟"轴，**照实报告**。
146	
147	### 5.2 E4 泛化
148	
149	- dev（in-domain）、tpl_ho（模板、goal、背景、PII 别名全部 held-out）、tool_ho（未见工具世界）分列。
150	- 预注册判据：I 档在 tpl_ho 上的下降幅度；tool_ho 的 safe-success。若崩溃，结论改写为"组合泛化仍是 open problem"。
151	
152	### 5.3 E5 校准（降级）
153	
154	- 用序列平均对数概率做 risk–coverage 曲线、ECE（以 safe_success 为正确性标签）。
155	- 不宣称"学会拒判"，直到 §4.4 的 A 档补齐。
156	
157	### 5.4 E6 planner 可移植性
158	
159	把同一编译输出喂给 ≥3 个 LLM planner（Qwen3-4B/8B、一个异家族模型），用同一检查器判 safe_success。只做推理，可在服务器上跑。
160	
161	### 5.5 E2/E3（GRPO，阶段 3）：前置条件与设计修正
162	
163	**前置条件**：v4 的规划世界已经提供独立的成功检查器，以及违反判定（RLVP 式的可验证规则），E2 的信息权限问题由此闭合：
164	- C* 只用于离线评测与 ② 的漏检罚。
165	- 所有臂拥有相同的信息权限。
166	- 训练用 train 世界，评测用 held-out。
167	
168	**臂（同预算，1.7B LoRA）**：
169	- vanilla GRPO
170	- ToolRLA 加法（λ=10）
171	- GDPO/ScAdv（按分量标准化）
172	- TAG 乘性门控（按其探针协议）
173	- RLVP 逐动作罚
174	- ②完整版
175	- ②去门控 / 去归因 / 对称罚
176	
177	**必报**：
178	- 四格（成功 × 满足）、反躺平三联、组内方差可达性预诊断（VarG）。
179	- 编译器噪声注入（FP/FN 各 3 档）存活曲线。
180	- 3 个 seed 加配对 bootstrap。
181	
182	**风险**：RLVP 明确写了 "chain 0.6B/1.7B (too weak)"。先测 1.7B 的 VarG 和 dead-update 比例，不达标就把 4B（QLoRA）作为主战场。
183	
184	### 5.6 统计纪律
185	
186	- 所有比较都在同一测试集上做**配对**检验：group bootstrap 1000 次以上，加精确 McNemar；多重比较做 Holm 校正。
187	- 种子：按用户要求主表统一 seed 42。论文里需要注明"单 seed + 数据层 bootstrap"。算力允许时，补 0.6B/1.7B 的 seed 43/44，作为训练方差估计。
188	- 预注册方向；不支持的结果照报；发散或中止的运行单列计数。
189

192	## 6. 代码审计结论
193	
194	| 项 | 结论 |
195	| --- | --- |
196	| completion-only loss | 正确：prefix 的 label 置 -100，completion 后接 EOS（`train_lora`） |
197	| NaN 防护 | 正确：前向 loss 有限性检查、`clip_grad_norm_(error_if_nonfinite=True)`、step 后参数有限性检查、bf16 加载、失败时写 `training_failure.json`。v4 smoke 的首步 loss 为 0.683，数值有限 |
198	| 截断丢样 | **已修**：v4 prompt 最长约 1060 token，原 max_seq 1024 会静默丢样本。改为 1280，并打印 dropped 数（smoke 中 12000/12000 保留） |
199	| 评分器 | v4 提交了 fail-closed 严格解析；v5 新增核心键（整值浮点按整数处理）、记录全对、N 误报率（显式计数） |
200	| 数据可复现 | **已修**：Windows 写盘为 CRLF，导致哈希跨平台不一致。现在显式写 LF，服务器重新生成后哈希相同 |
201	| 验证器自身 | v4 单测专门验证它能抓到篡改的 witness、N 版残留约束、held-out 工具泄漏。审计中发现并修正了一次 `\b` 被 shell 吞掉、导致指令词检查空过的问题 |
202	| 测试 | 本地 53 个全部通过（服务器的 conda 环境没有装 pytest；代码同一提交，已在本地跑过） |

206	## 7. 风险与工作量
207	
208	| 风险 | 触发 | 预案 |
209	| --- | --- | --- |
210	| v4 仍被 0.6B 打满 | dev/tpl_ho/tool_ho 的 safe-success 都 ≥0.99 | 仍有价值（对比 Z/P）。但应补改写 OOD 和外部 OOD，并加大 I 档的推理深度（三事实链） |
211	| T 输给强模型 PE | I 档或 tool_ho 上 T < P | 照报；叙事转向成本、延迟、本机部署 |
212	| 4B 显存或时间 | OOM 或单模型超过 12h | eval batch 已设为 16；必要时改用梯度检查点 |
213	| API 不稳定 | Codex 中转的 SSE 超时 | 断点续跑；Claude 中转作为主 P 臂 |
214	
215	时间估算（4080S）：每个模型 = zero-shot 评测 + 9000 步 + 训练后评测，0.6B 约 3–4h，1.7B 约 6–8h，4B 约 9–12h，三模型串行约 18–24h。P 臂、oracle、人审与 GPU 队列并行。
216	
217	---
218	
219	## 8. 禁止的表述
220	
221	- 用 v2/v3 或中期报告的任何数字。
222	- 拿解析 F1 当执行级安全成功率。
223	- 声称"三版语义等价"、"首次 scope 绑定/约束门控"、"零先例"。
224	- 说 tool_ho 证明了结构泛化（它只证明了未见名称和属性）。
225	- 在 E2 跑出结果之前声称 ② 有下游收益。
226	- 声称校准或拒判已经学会。

12	Abstract
13	LLM agents serve natural-language requests
14	through tools, data sources, and other agents,
15	and even simple requests often need several in-
16	terdependent calls. Typically, the LLM picks
17	these calls by trial and error, with no guarantee
18	of an executable plan. We present Capability-
19	Grounded Agentic Planning (CGAP), which in-
20	stead reasons about what a request requires and
21	what tools provide. CGAP compiles the tool
22	catalog deterministically into a PDDL model,
23	uses an LLM to turn the request into goals,
24	and solves the model with a classical planner.
25	Since tool outputs are unknown in advance, the
26	model is abstract, tracking which inputs are
27	available, not their values. During execution,
28	an LLM adds entity-specific calls that abstract
29	plans omit, and deterministic checks reject any
30	that break the plan. Every argument is drawn
31	from a cited source, such as a conversation span
32	or an earlier tool response, and each requested
33	result counts as delivered only after an LLM
34	verifier checks it against the request. With three
35	LLMs on ToolSandbox, ComplexFuncBench,
36	BFCL multi-turn, and τ 2-bench retail, CGAP
37	outperforms a standard tool-calling agent by up
38	to 28.9 points.
39	1
40	Introduction
41	LLM agents are increasingly used to retrieve infor-
42	mation and act on behalf of users through external
43	tools (Yao et al., 2023; Qin et al., 2024). How-
44	ever, both the tasks to solve and the tools that solve
45	them are described in natural language (NL), which
46	is imprecise and highly flexible. The LLM that
47	drives the agent must therefore both understand the
48	request and construct an executable plan for it, and
49	even simple requests require several interdependent
50	operations. For example, with basic forecasting,
51	date-lookup, and geolocation tools, a request for
52	the “weather in Paris and Nice next Monday, and
53	in Nice on Tuesday” takes seven calls: two city
54	lookups, two date resolutions, and three forecasts,
55	with the outputs of some calls supplying the inputs
56	of others.
57	ReAct-style agents address such problems by in-
58	terleaving reasoning with tool calls, choosing one
59	call at a time (Yao et al., 2023), while plan-first
60	systems such as HuggingGPT, ReWOO, and LLM-
61	Compiler write out a task decomposition or depen-
62	dency graph before acting (Shen et al., 2023; Xu
63	et al., 2023; Kim et al., 2024), a strategy that Plan-
64	and-Solve also applies to reasoning tasks (Wang
65	et al., 2023). However, both classes of approaches
66	use the LLM for both request interpretation and
67	planning, so nothing guarantees that a call’s in-
68	puts will be available when it runs. LLMs also
69	have documented limitations on formal planning
70	problems (Valmeekam et al., 2023), and intrinsic
71	self-correction can fail without external feedback
72	(Huang et al., 2024). LLM-based agentic workflow
73	planning therefore remains unreliable, particularly
74	with smaller (and cheaper) LLMs.
75	Hybrid (neuro-symbolic) alternatives combine
76	LLMs with formal planners.
77	Many, such as
78	LLM+P, use an LLM to translate a planning prob-
79	lem or action model into PDDL (McDermott et al.,
80	1998) for a classical planner (Liu et al., 2023; Guan
81	et al., 2023; Tantakoun et al., 2025), while LLM-
82	Modulo frameworks pair LLM proposals with ex-
83	ternal critics (Kambhampati et al., 2024). These
84	approaches start from actions that are described
85	formally or that the LLM writes down, and a plan
86	is only as valid as that model. Tool-using agents
87	instead work from NL specifications of requests
88	and tool capabilities, in an open world: the values
89	that their tools take and return are unknown until a
90	call returns, and they do not come from a finite set
91	that a symbolic planning model can enumerate.
92	We propose Capability-Grounded Agentic Plan-
93	ning (CGAP), a framework for agentic workflow
94	planning. CGAP reads the NL request together
95	with the catalog of capabilities available to the
96	agent, such as tools, data sources, or other agents,
97	1
98	arXiv:2610.41040v1  [cs.AI]  29 Oct 2026
99	
100	============================================================
101	=== PAGE 2 ===
102	============================================================
103	
104	each with an NL description and the input schema
105	that function-calling interfaces require; the LLM’s
106	own abilities, such as summarizing, are not mod-
107	eled as capabilities. CGAP compiles the catalog de-
108	terministically into a PDDL planning model, with
109	required inputs as preconditions and outputs as ef-
110	fects (§2.2), and an LLM parses the request into
111	one goal per requested result (§2.3). For open-
112	world inputs and outputs, the model abstracts away
113	values: it tracks only which named inputs and out-
114	puts (fields) are available, a finite set fixed by the
115	catalog. A classical planner solves this model, and
116	LLMs then turn the abstract plan into executable
117	calls and verify that their results match the request.
118	Our experiments test whether deriving the depen-
119	dencies between calls from this model improves
120	tool use over having an LLM generate them. We
121	instantiate the planner with state-space search, and
122	we also evaluate a deterministic dependency-graph
123	planner that ignores delete effects, to see how much
124	of the gain remains without them. Figure 1 shows
125	one user turn of this process.
126	In the weather example, the planner cannot pre-
127	dict what the tools will return, so the planning state
128	records only whether a value is available for a field
129	such as latitude, an output of the city lookup
130	and a required input of the forecast, and not which
131	city it describes. Each requested forecast is a sep-
132	arate goal, but one city lookup makes coordinates
133	available for every forecast, so the planner returns
134	a five-action abstract plan for a request that takes
135	seven calls (Figure 2). An execution LLM pro-
136	poses the entity-specific calls the plan omits, here a
137	lookup for Nice and a second date resolution, and
138	a deterministic runtime, which checks every call
139	before it runs, accepts such a proposal only if the
140	remaining plan stays valid. Every argument must
141	cite its source, so each coordinate can be traced to
142	the lookup that produced it, and a forecast counts
143	as delivered only after deterministic checks and an
144	LLM verifier accept the call that produced it.
145	We make three contributions:
146	• Neuro-symbolic agentic planning. CGAP, a
147	hybrid approach that compiles tool catalogs de-
148	terministically into an abstract, field-level PDDL
149	model that can be solved before tool outputs are
150	known, uses an LLM to turn the request into its
151	goals, and solves the model with classical plan-
152	ning (§2.2, §2.3).
153	• Checked execution with provable guarantees.
154	A runtime that validates the entity-specific calls
155	LLMs add, instantiates arguments from cited
156	sources, and verifies each requested result; every
157	execution it admits maps onto a valid abstract
158	plan, so exhaustive search failure certifies infea-
159	sibility for the compiled catalog (§2.5).
160	• Experiments on four tool-using agentic bench-

12	Abstract
13	LLM agents serve natural-language requests
14	through tools, data sources, and other agents,
15	and even simple requests often need several in-
16	terdependent calls. Typically, the LLM picks
17	these calls by trial and error, with no guarantee
18	of an executable plan. We present Capability-
19	Grounded Agentic Planning (CGAP), which in-
20	stead reasons about what a request requires and
21	what tools provide. CGAP compiles the tool
22	catalog deterministically into a PDDL model,
23	uses an LLM to turn the request into goals,
24	and solves the model with a classical planner.
25	Since tool outputs are unknown in advance, the
26	model is abstract, tracking which inputs are
27	available, not their values. During execution,
28	an LLM adds entity-specific calls that abstract
29	plans omit, and deterministic checks reject any
30	that break the plan. Every argument is drawn
31	from a cited source, such as a conversation span
32	or an earlier tool response, and each requested
33	result counts as delivered only after an LLM
34	verifier checks it against the request. With three
35	LLMs on ToolSandbox, ComplexFuncBench,
36	BFCL multi-turn, and τ 2-bench retail, CGAP
37	outperforms a standard tool-calling agent by up
38	to 28.9 points.
39	1
40	Introduction
41	LLM agents are increasingly used to retrieve infor-
42	mation and act on behalf of users through external
43	tools (Yao et al., 2023; Qin et al., 2024). How-
44	ever, both the tasks to solve and the tools that solve
45	them are described in natural language (NL), which
46	is imprecise and highly flexible. The LLM that
47	drives the agent must therefore both understand the
48	request and construct an executable plan for it, and
49	even simple requests require several interdependent
50	operations. For example, with basic forecasting,
51	date-lookup, and geolocation tools, a request for
52	the “weather in Paris and Nice next Monday, and
53	in Nice on Tuesday” takes seven calls: two city
54	lookups, two date resolutions, and three forecasts,
55	with the outputs of some calls supplying the inputs
56	of others.
57	ReAct-style agents address such problems by in-
58	terleaving reasoning with tool calls, choosing one
59	call at a time (Yao et al., 2023), while plan-first
60	systems such as HuggingGPT, ReWOO, and LLM-
61	Compiler write out a task decomposition or depen-
62	dency graph before acting (Shen et al., 2023; Xu
63	et al., 2023; Kim et al., 2024), a strategy that Plan-
64	and-Solve also applies to reasoning tasks (Wang
65	et al., 2023). However, both classes of approaches
66	use the LLM for both request interpretation and
67	planning, so nothing guarantees that a call’s in-
68	puts will be available when it runs. LLMs also
69	have documented limitations on formal planning
70	problems (Valmeekam et al., 2023), and intrinsic
71	self-correction can fail without external feedback
72	(Huang et al., 2024). LLM-based agentic workflow
73	planning therefore remains unreliable, particularly
74	with smaller (and cheaper) LLMs.
75	Hybrid (neuro-symbolic) alternatives combine
76	LLMs with formal planners.
77	Many, such as
78	LLM+P, use an LLM to translate a planning prob-
79	lem or action model into PDDL (McDermott et al.,
80	1998) for a classical planner (Liu et al., 2023; Guan
81	et al., 2023; Tantakoun et al., 2025), while LLM-
82	Modulo frameworks pair LLM proposals with ex-
83	ternal critics (Kambhampati et al., 2024). These
84	approaches start from actions that are described
85	formally or that the LLM writes down, and a plan
86	is only as valid as that model. Tool-using agents
87	instead work from NL specifications of requests
88	and tool capabilities, in an open world: the values
89	that their tools take and return are unknown until a
90	call returns, and they do not come from a finite set
91	that a symbolic planning model can enumerate.
92	We propose Capability-Grounded Agentic Plan-
93	ning (CGAP), a framework for agentic workflow
94	planning. CGAP reads the NL request together
95	with the catalog of capabilities available to the
96	agent, such as tools, data sources, or other agents,
97	1
98	arXiv:2610.41040v1  [cs.AI]  29 Oct 2026
99	
100	============================================================
101	=== PAGE 2 ===
102	============================================================
103	
104	each with an NL description and the input schema
105	that function-calling interfaces require; the LLM’s
106	own abilities, such as summarizing, are not mod-
107	eled as capabilities. CGAP compiles the catalog de-
108	terministically into a PDDL planning model, with
109	required inputs as preconditions and outputs as ef-
110	fects (§2.2), and an LLM parses the request into
111	one goal per requested result (§2.3). For open-
112	world inputs and outputs, the model abstracts away
113	values: it tracks only which named inputs and out-
114	puts (fields) are available, a finite set fixed by the
115	catalog. A classical planner solves this model, and
116	LLMs then turn the abstract plan into executable
117	calls and verify that their results match the request.
118	Our experiments test whether deriving the depen-
119	dencies between calls from this model improves
120	tool use over having an LLM generate them. We
121	instantiate the planner with state-space search, and
122	we also evaluate a deterministic dependency-graph
123	planner that ignores delete effects, to see how much
124	of the gain remains without them. Figure 1 shows
125	one user turn of this process.
126	In the weather example, the planner cannot pre-
127	dict what the tools will return, so the planning state
128	records only whether a value is available for a field
129	such as latitude, an output of the city lookup
130	and a required input of the forecast, and not which
131	city it describes. Each requested forecast is a sep-
132	arate goal, but one city lookup makes coordinates
133	available for every forecast, so the planner returns
134	a five-action abstract plan for a request that takes
135	seven calls (Figure 2). An execution LLM pro-
136	poses the entity-specific calls the plan omits, here a
137	lookup for Nice and a second date resolution, and
138	a deterministic runtime, which checks every call
139	before it runs, accepts such a proposal only if the
140	remaining plan stays valid. Every argument must
141	cite its source, so each coordinate can be traced to
142	the lookup that produced it, and a forecast counts
143	as delivered only after deterministic checks and an
144	LLM verifier accept the call that produced it.
145	We make three contributions:
146	• Neuro-symbolic agentic planning. CGAP, a
147	hybrid approach that compiles tool catalogs de-
148	terministically into an abstract, field-level PDDL
149	model that can be solved before tool outputs are
150	known, uses an LLM to turn the request into its
151	goals, and solves the model with classical plan-
152	ning (§2.2, §2.3).
153	• Checked execution with provable guarantees.
154	A runtime that validates the entity-specific calls
155	LLMs add, instantiates arguments from cited
156	sources, and verifies each requested result; every
157	execution it admits maps onto a valid abstract
158	plan, so exhaustive search failure certifies infea-
159	sibility for the compiled catalog (§2.5).
160	• Experiments on four tool-using agentic bench-
161	marks. With three LLMs on ToolSandbox, Com-
162	plexFuncBench, BFCL multi-turn, and τ 2-bench
163	retail, CGAP outperforms a standard tool-calling
164	agent in all 15 model–metric comparisons and,
165	with gpt-oss-20b, four further baselines.
166	Re-
167	placing deterministic dependency planning with
168	LLM-generated plans costs up to 16.8 points, less
169	with GPT-5 mini; a deterministic graph planner
170	retains most of the gain, and search adds to it
171	where actions have delete effects (§3).

806	We run each configuration three
807	times per task. Binary success metrics are aggre-
808	gated by majority (a task counts as solved if at least
809	two runs solve it), and ToolSandbox scores and
810	call accuracy are averaged over runs. Confidence
811	intervals use 10,000 task-level bootstrap resamples,
812	paired by task for differences between methods,

817	In Table 1, CGAP outperforms every baseline on
818	every benchmark and metric with all three LLMs,
819	and all 15 paired intervals against the plain agent
820	exclude zero (Table 4). The gains are smallest with
821	GPT-5 mini (5.1–13.9 points), whose plain agent
822	is the strongest on every metric.

824	most on state-dependency scenarios (98.4 against
825	62.8 with gpt-oss-20b; Table 5), which use our
826	hand-written device-dependency annotations. On
827	ComplexFuncBench, it improves success by 5.2–
828	10.8 points and call accuracy by 5.1–9.1, and on
829	BFCL multi-turn it gains 6.0–18.0 points. On τ 2-
830	bench retail, it gains 8.8–14.0 points although every
831	agent receives the same policy, both on the 64 tasks
832	involving two or more orders and on the other 50
833	(Table 6).

967	We presented CGAP, a neuro-symbolic approach in
968	which LLMs interpret requests, ground arguments,

17	Abstract
18	Tool-using LLM agents violate the policies they are deployed to enforce, often silently.
19	Prior defenses hand-write rules, query an LLM verifier per action, or compile policies
20	through heavyweight formal machinery. Naive compilation fails: extracted rules block the
21	tool satisfying their own precondition, or read arguments their tool lacks. NOMOS, a four-
22	pass compiler, turns a natural-language policy into a deterministic tool-call gate; static
23	verification with tool-schema-level checks alone (no prover, solver, or LLM) repairs or
24	rejects 37% (airline) and 13% (retail) of candidates, without which most shipped rules
25	are inoperable. Replaying compiled rules over undefended transcripts flags bindings that
26	refuse legitimate work (a development binding refused 95.9% of task-passing calls); no
27	evaluation binding is flagged. On τ 2-bench the gate cuts violations of reference-encoded
28	clauses among state-changing calls from 66.3% to 2.6% (airline) and 30.8% to 6.9% (retail),
29	raising airline task success significantly for 2 ≤k ≤4; a 26B on-premise compilation is
30	not significantly worse than hand-written or frontier-compiled rules. Unlike AgentDojo’s
31	shipped defenses, it reaches a zero attack success rate (ASR) on banking, where nine
32	attack families collapse onto three structural rules. On the other three suites its ASR is
33	at most 3.6%, from goals with no tool call to govern and one write admitted by a binding
34	weaker than its clause; a second agent model, Llama-3.3-70B, reproduces the effect on both
35	benchmarks. Decisions take microseconds without an LLM call, at a domain-dependent
36	benign-utility cost; compilation runs on-premise on open-weight gemma-4-26B.

2928	Limitations
2929	Our evidence is benchmark-scale: two τ 2-bench task-success
2930	domains (airline, retail) and all four AgentDojo injection
2931	suites. The safety effect is shown model-invariant across two
2932	agent models (gemma-4-26B and Llama-3.3-70B) on τ 2-
2933	bench airline and on all four AgentDojo suites, where the
2934	second model reproduces both the violation-rate reduction
2935	and the collapse of executed attacks to two travel pairs
2936	(Section 5.10); the τ 2-bench task-success results for retail
2937	use a single model, the second model’s workspace baseline
2938	is partial, and the injection evaluation uses AgentDojo’s
2939	standard and adaptive attacks rather than an exhaustive attack
2940	taxonomy.
2941	Residual violations under the gate (Table 5) are, with one
2942	exception, compiler coverage gaps; they are measurable (of
2943	the undefended baseline calls the reference sets refuse, the
2944	compiled sets refuse 97.4% on airline, 228 of 234, and
2945	80.5% on retail, 153 of 190) but not zero, and a clause the
2946	compiler misses is silently unenforced, which is why we
2947	measure compliance with an independent checker rather than
2948	claiming completeness. Retail shows that when violations
2949	do not corrupt scored state, the gate’s task-success benefit
2950	disappears (while its safety benefit remains).
2951	The fact store’s structural provenance depends on tools
2952	returning inspectable results; free-text-only tools would
2953	weaken it. The provenance boundary is also exactly the tool-
2954	result schema, and structured data inside that boundary is
2955	trusted: a policy clause that admits history-derived targets
2956	is only as strong as the process that writes the history, so
2957	an attacker who can place a value into a structured field the
2958	fact extractor reads, for example by seeding an unsolicited
2959	incoming transaction whose sender then appears as a known
2960	counterparty, poisons the allowlist without asserting anything
2961	in text. The AgentDojo attacks cannot exercise this path
2962	(injections edit free-text fields of existing records and cannot
2963	create them), so our results do not measure it; a deployment
2964	should treat clauses that admit discovered or history-derived
2965	targets as part of the attack surface and qualify them (di-
2966	rection, freshness, or explicit user confirmation) at policy-
2967	authoring time, qualifiers the compiler can carry into the
2968	predicate.
2969	The system also presupposes that a written policy exists:
2970	benchmarks generally do not ship one, so we authored the
2971	AgentDojo policies ourselves (regulated deployments, where
2972	written procedures already exist, face no such gap). On the
2973	messaging domain (slack), safety comes at a real utility
2974	cost because the benign task and the attack are structurally
2975	identical. The gate governs tool calls, not text: a policy about
2976	what the agent may say is out of scope.
2977	Finally, the implementation is proprietary and not released,
2978	which limits what a third party can verify directly; we

14	Abstract
15	Customer-service LLM agents must follow or-
16	ganizational policy when acting on a user’s be-

21	time safeguards can intervene on risky actions,

24	Workflow-
25	following systems support prescribed process

1171	Limitations
1172	Evaluation and validation.
1173	Our evaluation cov-
1174	ers all three English τ 2-bench customer-service
1175	domains (Barres et al., 2025), with four trials per
1176	multi-trial cell and three actor families on Air-
1177	line.
1178	The procedural audit complements final-
1179	state outcomes: two authors independently con-
1180	structed Telecom rules and event orders in blinded
1181	reviews, then discussed and cross-validated them
1182	(Appendix I.1). Process-valid success uses all 160
1183	task–trial pairs per condition.
1184	The supplemen-
1185	tary Call-NMR audit covers Airline and Retail;

1189	Broader policy regimes, languages, live users, and
1190	adaptive threats require setting-specific validation.
1191	Workflow generation and faithfulness.
1192	One
1193	frozen GPT 5.4-authored workflow per domain
1194	gives every system and actor family the same pol-
1195	icy representation, isolating runtime and executor
1196	differences from re-authoring. We manually veri-
1197	fied each graph against its source policy and tool
1198	specifications (Appendix E). This design supports
1199	a controlled comparison and tests workflow reuse
1200	across actors; generalization of workflow authoring
1201	across models or seeds is a separate question.
1202	Trigger and cost.
1203	User-turn verification proac-
1204	tively guides procedural steps beyond mutating
1205	calls, while the corrective intercept preserves the ac-
1206	tor’s execution loop for remediation. The advisory
1207	write gate disarms after interception and rearms at
1208	the next user turn. Appendix I characterizes this
1209	behavior under forced retries, corrective-verifier
1210	exceptions, and repeated transfers. The cadence
1211	concentrates verification at specified boundaries;
1212	broader event coverage requires more verifier calls.
1213	Guide fees are approximately $0.40 per conversa-
1214	tion; Appendix D reports call counts, fees, and ob-

16	Abstract
17	Existing tool-augmented large language models (LLMs) en-
18	counter significant challenges when processing complex
19	queries. Current frameworks such as ReAct are prone to
20	local optimization traps due to their reliance on incremen-
21	tal decision-making processes. To address these limitations,
22	we propose a novel Planner-centric Plan-Execute paradigm
23	that fundamentally resolves local optimization bottlenecks
24	through architectural innovation. Central to our approach is
25	a novel Planner model that performs global Directed Acyclic
26	Graph (DAG) planning for complex queries, enabling opti-
27	mized execution beyond conventional tool coordination. We
28	also introduce ComplexTool-Plan, a large-scale benchmark
29	dataset featuring complex queries that demand sophisticated
30	multi-tool composition and coordination capabilities. Addi-
31	tionally, we develop a two-stage training methodology that in-
32	tegrates Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with Group Relative
33	Policy Optimization (GRPO), systematically enhancing the
34	Planner’s tool selection accuracy and global planning aware-
35	ness through structured DAG-based planning. When inte-
36	grated with a capable executor, our framework achieves state-
37	of-the-art performance on the StableToolBench benchmark
38	for complex user queries, demonstrating superior end-to-end
39	execution capabilities and robust handling of intricate multi-
40	tool workflows. Our code and data are publicly available at
41	https://github.com/weixiaolong94-hub/Beyond-React.
42	Introduction
43	Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated re-
44	markable prowess in language processing, yet their inherent
45	knowledge is static and they lack direct interaction with the
46	external world. A transformative solution is tool augmenta-
47	tion, which empowers LLMs to act as autonomous agents
48	by calling external APIs and tools (Schick et al. 2023; Patil
49	et al. 2024). This paradigm shifts LLMs from being mere
50	text generators to active problem-solvers capable of tack-
51	ling complex, real-world tasks, a trend exemplified by sys-
52	tems like HuggingGPT (Shen et al. 2023) and the rise of
53	multi-agent frameworks (Hong et al. 2023). The evaluation

67	(Yao et al. 2023b), often augmented by self-reflection tech-

69	from inherent local optimization traps due to its incremen-

374	Experimental Setup
375	Dataset
376	We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of our framework
377	from two primary perspectives: (1) the quality of the gen-
378
